definition: Oriented FAST and rotated BRIEF (ORB) is a fast robust local feature detector, first presented by Ethan Rublee et al.
details: in 2011, that can be used in computer vision tasks like object recognition or 3D reconstruction. It is based on the FAST keypoint detector and a modified version of the visual descriptor BRIEF (Binary Robust Independent Elementary Features). Its aim is to provide a fast and efficient alternative to SIFT.

explainer.lead: Oriented FAST and rotated BRIEF is a fast, robust local feature detector for computer vision tasks like object recognition and 3D reconstruction. It matters as a fast and efficient alternative to SIFT.

tiers.eli5: It picks out distinctive spots in a picture and describes them so the same spot can be recognised again, even from another angle.
tiers.practitioner: It builds on the FAST keypoint detector and a modified version of the BRIEF descriptor. A pitfall is expecting SIFT-level behaviour, since its stated aim is to be a faster, more efficient alternative rather than the same method.
tiers.paperLevel: Presented by Ethan Rublee et al. in 2011; based on the FAST keypoint detector and a modified version of the BRIEF visual descriptor, aiming to provide a fast and efficient alternative to SIFT.

explainer.example: A robot matches features between two photos of the same object taken from different viewpoints using ORB keypoints and descriptors to support 3D reconstruction.
